target: FAKE TEST PRODUCT — 'Acme Billing' exists only as Scruffy's built-in repair fixture; no finding here describes a real app

run.authority_basis: The request authorized implementation of approved fixes.

items.plain: Three billing surfaces calculate the same invoice differently, so customers can receive conflicting totals.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Billing state is computed inside the view
items.observation: The invoice total, tax, and dunning state are derived in the render function; three surfaces recompute them differently.
items.user_impact: Totals disagree between the summary, the PDF, and the email, so users cannot trust any of them.
evidence: Three divergent total computations across BillingSummary, invoicePdf, and dunningEmail
items.cause: No single billing-state module; each surface recomputes from raw rows.
items.recommendation: Extract one billing-state module that returns total, tax, and dunning state; have all surfaces read it.
acceptance_checks: A single module is the only source of invoice total, tax, and dunning state
Summary, PDF, and email render identical totals for the same invoice

items.plain: The past-due label is too faint to read reliably even though it carries the page's most important state.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Payment-status pill fails contrast
items.observation: The 'Past due' pill renders #b9895f on #f2efe9 at 2.4:1, below WCAG 1.4.3.
items.user_impact: Low-vision users cannot read the single most important billing state.
evidence: Measured contrast ratio 2.4:1 on the status pill
items.cause: Muted decorative token reused for a critical status.
items.recommendation: Use a status color token that meets 4.5:1 against the pill background.
acceptance_checks: The 'Past due' pill text meets at least 4.5:1 contrast
The status is distinguishable without relying on color alone

items.plain: Retrying a payment produces no pending, success, or failure feedback, leaving customers unsure whether anything happened.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Retry-payment button gives no feedback
items.observation: Pressing 'Retry payment' shows no pending, success, or failure state; the row is unchanged.
items.user_impact: Users press retry repeatedly, unsure whether a charge was attempted.
evidence: Operated the retry flow; no state change on the row
items.cause: The handler awaits the request but never reflects pending or result state.
items.recommendation: Give retry a pending state, then a success or failure result the row reflects.
acceptance_checks: Retry shows a pending state while the request is in flight
Success and failure each produce a distinct, announced row state

items.plain: Every plan uses the same vague benefit sentence, so customers cannot tell what changes with price.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Plan descriptions are interchangeable filler
items.observation: Each plan reads 'Powerful features to help your team do more,' with no concrete difference.
items.user_impact: Users cannot tell the plans apart at the moment they choose one.
evidence: Three plan cards share one interchangeable benefit sentence
items.cause: Placeholder marketing copy was never replaced with real plan differences.
items.recommendation: Replace each plan's sentence with the concrete limit or capability that distinguishes it.
acceptance_checks: Each plan names a concrete, checkable difference from the others
No two plan descriptions remain interchangeable

manual_checks.evidence: Benefit claim is identical across differently priced plans.

editorial_review.consequence: The reader cannot differentiate plans at the point of choice.
editorial_review.counterexample_tested: Not legitimate genre shorthand: the sentence is identical across paid tiers.

items.plain: A decorative gradient competes with the balance due, weakening the hierarchy of the billing page.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Arbitrary hero gradient weakens hierarchy
items.observation: The billing hero uses a decorative purple-to-orange gradient unrelated to any state.
items.user_impact: The gradient competes with the balance-due figure for attention.
evidence: Rendered hero draws the eye away from the primary figure
items.recommendation: Remove the gradient; let the balance-due figure lead.
acceptance_checks: The balance-due figure is the clear first fixation in the hero

items.plain: Customers in dark environments could benefit from an optional low-light theme after the approved repairs are complete.
items.title: [FIXTURE] Offer a dark theme
items.user_impact: Users in dark environments have no low-light option.
items.recommendation: Add a dark theme once tokens are consolidated.
acceptance_checks: A dark theme is selectable and passes contrast
